questions.stem: The Yoruba people trace their origin and ancestry to which legendary figure?
questions.explanation: Oduduwa is regarded as the progenitor and ancestor of the Yoruba people, believed to have descended from Ile-Ife, the cradle of Yoruba civilization.

questions.stem: The ancient city of Ile-Ife is most significant in Yoruba history because it is considered the
questions.explanation: Ile-Ife is regarded as the spiritual and ancestral home from which the Yoruba people and, according to some traditions, all of humanity originated.

questions.stem: The Hausa states that existed before 1800 are collectively referred to as
questions.explanation: The seven original Hausa states-Biram, Daura, Gobir, Kano, Katsina, Rano, and Zazzau-are collectively called Hausa Bakwai, meaning the seven true Hausa states.

questions.stem: According to Hausa legend, which figure founded the Hausa states by slaying a sacred snake?
questions.explanation: Bayajidda, a prince from Baghdad according to legend, slew the sacred snake of Daura and married Queen Daura, and his descendants went on to found the Hausa states.

questions.stem: The Igbo people are predominantly found in which geopolitical zone of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Igbo are one of the largest ethnic groups in Nigeria and are predominantly located in the South-Eastern states such as Anambra, Enugu, Imo, Ebonyi, and Abia.

questions.stem: The Igbo political system before 1800 is best described as
questions.explanation: The Igbo practiced a largely acephalous (stateless) political system with decision-making vested in age grades, councils of elders, and title societies, making it decentralized and republican in nature.

questions.stem: The Benin Kingdom, known for its bronze art, was ruled by
questions.explanation: The Benin Kingdom was governed by divine monarchs known as Obas. The Oba of Benin was both the political and spiritual leader of the kingdom.

questions.stem: Benin bronze sculptures are historically significant primarily because they

options.A: demonstrate advanced artistic and technological skills of pre-colonial Nigeria
options.C: were religious items imported from Europe

questions.explanation: The Benin bronzes are world-renowned works of art that showcase the sophisticated craftsmanship, metallurgical knowledge, and cultural complexity of the Benin Kingdom long before European contact.

questions.stem: The Nok Culture is important in Nigerian history because it produced

options.A: the earliest known terracotta sculptures in sub-Saharan Africa
options.B: the first iron smelting in West Africa
options.C: the oldest written records in Nigeria

questions.explanation: The Nok Culture, dating from around 1500 BCE to 500 CE in present-day central Nigeria, is renowned for producing the earliest known terracotta figurines in sub-Saharan Africa.

questions.stem: The Kanem-Borno Empire was located around which major geographic feature?
questions.explanation: The Kanem-Borno Empire rose around the Lake Chad basin in northeastern Nigeria and surrounding regions, and was one of the longest-surviving states in African history.

questions.stem: Islam was introduced into the Hausa states primarily through
questions.explanation: Islam spread into the Hausa states from the 14th century onward largely through the activities of Muslim traders and scholars traveling along trans-Saharan trade routes.

questions.stem: The Yoruba art of Ile-Ife was particularly noted for producing realistic
questions.explanation: Ile-Ife produced remarkably naturalistic bronze and terracotta heads that are considered some of the finest examples of African classical art, dating from around the 12th-14th centuries.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an ethnic minority group in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Ijaw (Izon) are one of the largest ethnic minority groups in Nigeria and are predominantly found in the Niger Delta region, with a culture deeply tied to the waterways.

questions.stem: The Oyo Empire rose to prominence largely due to its
questions.explanation: The Oyo Empire expanded its territory through a powerful cavalry force, which gave it a military advantage over neighboring states across the savanna region of West Africa.

questions.stem: The title given to the traditional ruler of Oyo Empire is
questions.explanation: The supreme ruler of the Oyo Empire bore the title Alaafin of Oyo. The Alaafin was considered a divine king whose authority was balanced by the Oyo Mesi council.

questions.stem: The Arochukwu Oracle, known as the Long Juju, was associated with which ethnic group?
questions.explanation: The Arochukwu Oracle (Ibini Ukpabi or Long Juju) was a powerful religious and economic institution of the Aro subgroup of the Igbo people, used to adjudicate disputes and facilitate the slave trade.

questions.stem: Traditional Yoruba religion is based on the worship of
questions.explanation: The Yoruba traditional religion (often called Ifa or Orisha worship) centers on a pantheon of spiritual beings called Orishas, who serve as intermediaries between Olodumare (the Supreme God) and humanity.

questions.stem: The Igbo concept of 'Chi' refers to
questions.explanation: In Igbo belief, 'Chi' is an individual's personal spirit or divine counterpart assigned at birth, which shapes their destiny and fortune throughout life.

questions.stem: Which group of people founded the Kanem-Borno Empire?
questions.explanation: The Kanem-Borno Empire was founded and ruled primarily by the Kanuri people under the Sayfawa dynasty, which was one of the longest-reigning dynasties in world history.

questions.stem: The system of government practiced by the Hausa states before the Jihad was mainly

options.A: emirate system with Sarki as ruler

questions.explanation: Before the Fulani Jihad of 1804, Hausa states were ruled by kings called Sarki (plural: Sarakuna), who governed through a hierarchical administrative system.

questions.stem: Social norms are rules that provide a standard by which conduct is
questions.explanation: Social norms serve as the evaluative criteria against which human behavior and conduct within a society are assessed and judged.

questions.stem: The term 'values' in social science refers to

options.A: deeply held beliefs about what is good and desirable

questions.explanation: Values are internalized principles or standards of behavior that individuals and societies consider important, guiding judgments about what is good, right, and desirable.

questions.stem: Which of the following best distinguishes a norm from a value?

options.A: Norms are specific behavioral expectations; values are broader ideals
options.B: Norms are laws; values are customs
options.C: Norms are personal; values are social
options.D: Norms are religious; values are secular

questions.explanation: Values are abstract ideals (e.g., honesty, justice), while norms are the specific rules of behavior that reflect and enforce those values in everyday social life.

questions.stem: Sanctions in the context of social norms refer to

options.A: rewards or punishments used to enforce conformity

questions.explanation: Sanctions are the mechanisms-positive (rewards) or negative (punishments)-through which societies enforce adherence to established norms.

questions.stem: A 'folkway' is best described as

options.A: a customary way of behaving with no serious moral significance
options.B: a law enforced by the state

questions.explanation: Folkways, as defined by sociologist William Graham Sumner, are routine conventions of everyday life (like table manners) that carry no strong moral weight but guide social interaction.

questions.stem: Mores differ from folkways primarily in that mores

options.A: carry strong moral significance and violation is considered serious
options.C: are only applicable to the elderly

questions.explanation: Mores are norms that are considered essential to the welfare of society and carry strong moral connotations; their violation is regarded as a serious offense.

questions.stem: The process by which individuals learn and internalize the norms and values of their society is called
questions.explanation: Socialization is the lifelong process through which individuals acquire the cultural norms, values, beliefs, and behaviors necessary for participating in their society.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a positive sanction?

options.A: Giving an award for excellent performance

questions.explanation: Positive sanctions are rewards given to reinforce desirable behavior. An award for excellent performance encourages conformity to valued social standards.

questions.stem: When an individual's personal values conflict with the values of their society, this is referred to as
questions.explanation: Value conflict occurs when an individual's internalized personal values clash with the broader values or expectations held by their social group or society.

questions.stem: Integrity as a value means

options.A: adherence to moral and ethical principles

questions.explanation: Integrity refers to the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles; it involves consistency between one's values, words, and actions.

questions.stem: Respect for elders in Nigerian societies is an example of a
questions.explanation: Respecting elders is a deeply embedded cultural value across many Nigerian ethnic groups, reflecting beliefs about seniority, wisdom, and social hierarchy.

questions.stem: Taboos are norms that

options.A: strictly prohibit certain behaviors considered sacred or dangerous

questions.explanation: Taboos are strong social prohibitions relating to any area of human activity that is considered sacred or forbidden, violation of which typically results in severe social or spiritual consequences.

questions.stem: The role of family as an agent of socialization is to

options.A: transmit primary values and norms to children

questions.explanation: The family is considered the primary agent of socialization, being the first and most influential institution through which children learn language, values, norms, and expected behaviors.

questions.stem: Honesty, hard work, and patriotism are examples of
questions.explanation: Honesty, hard work, and patriotism are positive values that societies uphold as desirable character traits and behavioral standards for their members.

questions.stem: The trans-Saharan trade route primarily connected West Africa with

options.A: North Africa and the Mediterranean world

questions.explanation: The trans-Saharan trade routes linked the kingdoms and states of West Africa, including those in present-day Nigeria, with North African cities like Tripoli, Tunis, and Cairo, and through them with the Mediterranean world.

questions.stem: The major commodities exported from the Hausa states through the trans-Saharan trade included

options.A: kola nuts, leather goods, and slaves

questions.explanation: Hausa traders exported kola nuts, leather goods (Moroccan leather), cloth, and enslaved people northward across the Sahara in exchange for salt, horses, and imported goods.

questions.stem: The introduction of the cowrie shell as a medium of exchange in pre-colonial Nigeria served as
questions.explanation: Cowrie shells were widely used as a standardized medium of exchange across many parts of pre-colonial Nigeria and West Africa, functioning effectively as currency in local and long-distance trade.

questions.stem: The concept of self-reliance in Nigerian economic history refers to

options.A: the ability to produce and sustain livelihoods through local resources

questions.explanation: Self-reliance means developing and utilizing indigenous resources, skills, and systems to meet the economic needs of individuals and the nation without excessive dependence on external sources.

questions.stem: The earliest form of trade in Nigerian history was
questions.explanation: Before the introduction of currency, trade in Nigerian societies was conducted through barter-the direct exchange of goods and services for other goods and services of equivalent value.

questions.stem: Kano was historically significant as a commercial center because it was

options.A: a major hub of trans-Saharan and intra-regional trade

questions.explanation: Kano was one of the most important commercial cities in pre-colonial West Africa, serving as a crossroads for trans-Saharan and regional trade with thriving markets, crafts, and textile industries.

questions.stem: The groundnut pyramids of northern Nigeria were a symbol of
questions.explanation: The towering groundnut pyramids of Kano were physical representations of Nigeria's agricultural wealth in the post-independence era, with groundnuts being a major export crop that brought foreign exchange earnings.

questions.stem: The Nigerian economy before colonialism was primarily based on
questions.explanation: Pre-colonial Nigerian economies were largely agrarian, with communities engaged in farming, fishing, animal husbandry, craftsmanship, and trade as the main economic activities.

questions.stem: The Royal Niger Company was established primarily to

options.A: control trade along the River Niger for British commercial interests

questions.explanation: The Royal Niger Company, chartered in 1886, was a British commercial enterprise that controlled trade along the Niger River and used its economic dominance to lay the foundation for British colonial control of Nigeria.

questions.stem: Palm oil became a major export commodity from southern Nigeria in the 19th century primarily because of

options.A: the industrial revolution in Europe creating demand for lubricants

questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution in Europe created enormous demand for palm oil as a lubricant for machinery and a raw material for soap manufacturing, transforming it into southern Nigeria's most valuable export.

questions.stem: The formal amalgamation of the Northern and Southern Protectorates of Nigeria took place in
questions.explanation: On January 1, 1914, Lord Frederick Lugard amalgamated the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria and the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria into a single administrative unit called Nigeria.

questions.stem: The policy of Indirect Rule in Nigeria was designed by
questions.explanation: Lord Frederick Lugard developed and implemented the policy of Indirect Rule in Northern Nigeria, using existing traditional rulers and institutions as intermediaries for British colonial administration.

questions.stem: Indirect Rule in the north was more effective than in the south primarily because

options.A: the north had established centralized emirate systems that could be used
options.B: southerners were hostile to all governance

questions.explanation: The highly organized and centralized emirate political structures of the north, with clear hierarchies of authority, were ideal vehicles for implementing Indirect Rule. The south's more decentralized, often stateless societies lacked comparable institutions.

questions.stem: The War Against Indiscipline (WAI) was launched in Nigeria in 1984 by
questions.explanation: WAI was launched by the military government of General Muhammadu Buhari in 1984 to address what the government saw as widespread indiscipline, corruption, and social vices in Nigerian society.

questions.stem: The Berlin Conference of 1884-1885 is significant in Nigerian history because it

options.A: formalized the partition of Africa among European powers

questions.explanation: The Berlin Conference (also called the Congo Conference) established the rules for the European colonization and partition of Africa, directly leading to the formal boundaries and control structures that defined colonial Nigeria.

questions.stem: The Aba Women's Riot of 1929 was a protest against

options.A: feared taxation of women by colonial authorities

questions.explanation: The Aba Women's Riots (also called the Women's War or Ogu Umunwanyi) erupted in 1929 when Igbo women feared they would be subjected to direct taxation by the colonial government, leading to a massive uprising.

questions.stem: The Richard's Constitution of 1946 was significant because it

options.A: introduced regional councils and laid groundwork for regionalism
options.C: unified Nigeria for the first time

questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution introduced the framework of regionalism into Nigerian governance by establishing North, East, and West regional councils, which later became the basis for Nigeria's federal structure.

questions.stem: Nigeria gained its independence from Britain on
questions.explanation: Nigeria officially gained independence from British colonial rule on October 1, 1960, which is now celebrated annually as Nigeria's Independence Day.

questions.stem: The Cash Crop policy under British colonial rule required Nigerian farmers to

options.A: grow export crops like groundnuts, cotton, and cocoa for British markets
options.B: grow food crops for local consumption

questions.explanation: British colonial economic policy encouraged or compelled Nigerian farmers to cultivate cash crops such as groundnuts, palm oil, cotton, cocoa, and rubber primarily for export to meet the raw material needs of British industries.

questions.stem: The policy of 'assimilation' in French colonial Africa differed from British Indirect Rule in that assimilation aimed to

options.A: transform Africans into French citizens by adopting French culture
options.B: preserve African traditions and use them for governance

questions.explanation: French colonial policy of assimilation sought to culturally transform Africans into French subjects by imposing French language, culture, and legal norms, unlike the British policy of Indirect Rule which sought to govern Africans through their own modified institutions.

questions.stem: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 was notable for introducing

options.A: an elective principle allowing some Nigerians to vote for representatives

questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 was the first to introduce an elective principle in Nigeria, allowing a limited number of educated Nigerians in Lagos and Calabar to elect representatives to the Legislative Council.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian nationalist famously described the amalgamation of Nigeria as a 'mistake of 1914'?
questions.explanation: Chief Obafemi Awolowo, a prominent Nigerian nationalist and politician, expressed in his writings that the forced amalgamation of different peoples into one Nigerian state was a historical mistake.

questions.stem: The 3Rs in Nigerian national re-orientation stand for
questions.explanation: The 3Rs policy was introduced after the Nigerian Civil War (1967-1970) by General Yakubu Gowon to guide the reintegration of the Igbo and other affected communities: Reconstruction of destroyed infrastructure, Rehabilitation of displaced persons, and Reconciliation of divided groups.

questions.stem: Operation Feed the Nation (OFN) was launched in Nigeria in 1976 by
questions.explanation: Operation Feed the Nation was launched in May 1976 by General Olusegun Obasanjo's military government to encourage Nigerians to grow their own food, reduce reliance on food imports, and boost agricultural production.

questions.stem: The Green Revolution in Nigeria was a policy introduced by
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution was introduced by President Shehu Shagari's civilian government in 1980 as a comprehensive agricultural development program aimed at achieving food self-sufficiency and reducing Nigeria's dependence on food imports.

questions.stem: The primary objective of the Green Revolution in Nigeria was to

options.A: achieve food self-sufficiency and revitalize agriculture

questions.explanation: The Green Revolution aimed to boost Nigeria's agricultural sector through improved farming techniques, modern inputs, and government support, with the ultimate goal of achieving food security and self-sufficiency.

questions.stem: Austerity measures introduced in Nigeria in the early 1980s were primarily a response to

options.A: falling oil prices and dwindling foreign exchange reserves

questions.explanation: As global oil prices collapsed in the early 1980s, Nigeria's oil-dependent economy suffered severe revenue shortfalls, forcing the government to introduce austerity measures including import restrictions and public expenditure cuts.

questions.stem: One of the key activities associated with the War Against Indiscipline (WAI) was

options.A: queuing culture enforcement and environmental sanitation

questions.explanation: WAI focused on instilling orderly public behavior, including enforcing queuing at bus stops and public places, proper waste disposal, punctuality, and other civic responsibilities.

questions.stem: The War Against Indiscipline and Corruption (WAIC) was an extension of WAI launched under
questions.explanation: WAIC was introduced by General Ibrahim Babangida's administration as an expanded version of WAI, adding an explicit anti-corruption dimension to the earlier campaign against social indiscipline.

questions.stem: The National Orientation Agency (NOA) was established primarily to

options.A: promote civic consciousness and national values among Nigerians

questions.explanation: The National Orientation Agency was created to sensitize, educate, and mobilize Nigerians toward patriotism, civic responsibility, national unity, and the internalization of core national values.

questions.stem: Operation Feed the Nation aimed primarily to

options.A: encourage citizens to cultivate food and reduce dependence on food imports
options.B: distribute free food to the poor

questions.explanation: OFN was a mass mobilization campaign urging all Nigerians, including urban dwellers, to participate in food production through backyard and community farming to reduce the food import bill.

questions.stem: Re-orientation strategies in Nigeria are designed to

options.A: change negative attitudes and behaviors toward positive national values

questions.explanation: National re-orientation strategies seek to reshape the attitudes, values, and behaviors of citizens, correcting tendencies such as corruption, indiscipline, and tribalism in favor of positive values that promote national development.

questions.stem: Austerity measures typically include all of the following EXCEPT

options.A: increased government spending on social programs

questions.explanation: Austerity measures involve reducing government spending, cutting subsidies, restricting imports, and other cost-cutting approaches to manage economic difficulties-they are the opposite of increased public spending.

questions.stem: The 3Rs policy after the Nigerian Civil War was meant to address the needs of
questions.explanation: The 3Rs (Reconstruction, Rehabilitation, Reconciliation) policy was specifically designed to heal the wounds of the 1967-1970 Civil War by rebuilding infrastructure, reintegrating ex-Biafran citizens, and promoting national unity.

questions.stem: The name 'Nigeria' was coined by
questions.explanation: The name 'Nigeria' was suggested by Flora Shaw, a journalist (later Lady Lugard, wife of Frederick Lugard), in an article published in The Times of London in 1897, referring to the territory around the River Niger.

questions.stem: The Protectorate of Northern Nigeria was created in
questions.explanation: On January 1, 1900, the British government formally established the Protectorate of Northern Nigeria, with Lord Frederick Lugard as its first High Commissioner, replacing the Royal Niger Company's administration.

questions.stem: Nigeria became a Republic on
questions.explanation: Nigeria became a Federal Republic on October 1, 1963, replacing the Queen of England as head of state with a Nigerian President (Nnamdi Azikiwe), while remaining within the Commonwealth.

questions.stem: The first military coup in Nigeria occurred on
questions.explanation: Nigeria's first military coup took place on January 15, 1966, when a group of army majors led by Major Chukwuma Kaduna Nzeogwu overthrew the civilian government, killing several prominent political leaders.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Civil War lasted from
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Civil War (also known as the Biafran War) was fought between the Nigerian federal government and the secessionist Republic of Biafra from July 6, 1967 to January 15, 1970.

questions.stem: The declaration of the Republic of Biafra was made by
questions.explanation: Colonel Odumegwu Ojukwu, military governor of Eastern Nigeria, declared the independence of the Republic of Biafra on May 30, 1967, triggering the Nigerian Civil War.

questions.stem: Nigeria's federal structure was formally established by the
questions.explanation: The Lyttleton Constitution (MacPherson's successor) of 1954 formally established Nigeria as a federation with three regions (North, East, West), each with its own government, marking a decisive move toward federalism.

questions.stem: The policy of 'No Victor, No Vanquished' after the Civil War was declared by
questions.explanation: After the end of the Civil War in 1970, General Yakubu Gowon proclaimed 'No Victor, No Vanquished' as the foundation of his reconciliation policy, emphasizing that all Nigerians were equal citizens regardless of which side they had supported.

questions.stem: The first indigenous Governor-General of Nigeria was
questions.explanation: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe became Nigeria's first indigenous (Nigerian-born) Governor-General on November 16, 1960, and later became the first President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria in 1963.

questions.stem: Nigeria's first Prime Minister at independence was
questions.explanation: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa became Nigeria's first and only Prime Minister at independence on October 1, 1960. He was assassinated during the military coup of January 15, 1966.

questions.stem: The transition from military to civilian rule in 1979 resulted in

options.A: Shehu Shagari becoming Nigeria's first executive president

questions.explanation: General Olusegun Obasanjo handed over power to democratically elected Shehu Shagari on October 1, 1979, making Shagari Nigeria's first executive president under the American-style presidential constitution.

questions.stem: The creation of states in Nigeria from the original regions was first done under
questions.explanation: General Yakubu Gowon created 12 states from the existing 4 regions on May 27, 1967, just days before the outbreak of the Civil War, partly to undermine Biafra's claim to represent all Eastern minorities.

questions.stem: The Sokoto Caliphate was established following the Jihad led by
questions.explanation: Usman dan Fodio (Shehu Usman dan Fodio) launched a jihad in 1804 against the Hausa rulers, establishing the Sokoto Caliphate by 1808-one of the largest states in 19th-century Africa.

questions.stem: The primary grievance of Usman dan Fodio against the Hausa rulers was

options.A: corruption and the mixing of Islam with traditional practices

questions.explanation: Dan Fodio criticized the Hausa rulers for their corruption, tyranny, unjust taxation, and syncretistic religious practices that blended Islam with traditional Hausa beliefs, which he considered un-Islamic.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the concept of national unity in the Nigerian context?

options.A: The coexistence and cooperation of Nigeria's diverse ethnic groups as one nation
options.B: Uniformity of culture across all ethnic groups
options.C: A single religion for all Nigerians
options.D: The dominance of one ethnic group

questions.explanation: National unity in Nigeria refers to the forging of a cohesive national identity and sense of common purpose among Nigeria's over 250 ethnic groups, respecting diversity while pursuing shared national goals.

questions.stem: The Efik people of Calabar were historically known for their role in

options.A: the Atlantic slave trade and later legitimate palm oil trade

questions.explanation: The Efik of Calabar were major middlemen in the Atlantic slave trade, using their strategic location at the Cross River estuary. After abolition, they successfully transitioned to trading palm oil and other commodities.

questions.stem: The concept of 'Omoluabi' in Yoruba culture represents

options.A: a person of good character, integrity, and moral rectitude

questions.explanation: Omoluabi is the Yoruba ideal of a well-bred, morally upright person who embodies good character (iwa pele), respect, hard work, honesty, and all the positive values that Yoruba society esteems.

questions.stem: The Ifa divination system is associated with which ethnic group?
questions.explanation: Ifa is a Yoruba divination system and body of literary corpus recognized by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. It is practiced by babalawos (diviners) to communicate with the deity Orunmila.

questions.stem: The Igbo masquerade (Mmanwu) is primarily understood as

options.A: ancestral spirits manifesting in the human world

questions.explanation: In Igbo culture, the Mmanwu (masquerade) represents the spirits of ancestors returning from the land of the dead. They serve social, judicial, and entertainment functions in Igbo communities.

questions.stem: Which colonial structure was responsible for administering Nigeria between 1886 and 1900?
questions.explanation: The Royal Niger Company, chartered by the British government in 1886, held administrative and commercial control over the Niger territories from 1886 until 1900 when the British government took direct control.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Youth Movement (NYM) founded in 1934 was significant because it

options.A: was the first truly nationalist political organization in Nigeria

questions.explanation: The Nigerian Youth Movement was one of Nigeria's earliest and most important nationalist organizations, advocating for greater Nigerian participation in governance and opposing British colonial policies.

questions.stem: The Indirect Rule system failed in the Igbo areas mainly because

options.A: the Igbo had no centralized traditional authority structures that could be used
options.B: the Igbo refused all contact with the British
options.C: the British did not attempt to apply it
options.D: the Igbo had their own colonial system

questions.explanation: The Igbo's decentralized, acephalous political system lacked the paramount chiefs and centralized authorities needed for Indirect Rule to work. The British had to create 'warrant chiefs', which proved deeply unpopular and led to the 1929 Women's War.

questions.stem: The Structural Adjustment Program (SAP) introduced in Nigeria in 1986 was meant to

options.A: reform the economy through deregulation, privatization, and reduced government spending

questions.explanation: SAP, introduced under General Ibrahim Babangida in 1986 under IMF/World Bank guidance, aimed to restructure Nigeria's ailing economy through currency devaluation, removal of subsidies, privatization, and trade liberalization.

questions.stem: Patriotism as a national value requires citizens to

options.A: love and serve their country with dedication and loyalty
options.C: prioritize personal wealth over national interest

questions.explanation: Patriotism involves a deep love for one's country, a sense of pride in its heritage, and a commitment to contributing to its progress and welfare, even at personal cost.

questions.stem: The 'scramble for Africa' refers to

options.A: the rapid colonization of Africa by European powers in the late 19th century
options.D: the spread of Islam in Africa

questions.explanation: The Scramble for Africa describes the rush by European nations-Britain, France, Germany, Belgium, Portugal, Italy, and Spain-to colonize African territories between approximately 1881 and 1914.

questions.stem: The National Orientation Agency (NOA) operates under which federal ministry?

options.A: Ministry of Information and National Orientation

questions.explanation: The National Orientation Agency operates under the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation, as its mandate is closely tied to public communication, civic education, and national values promotion.

questions.stem: The concept of 'Nchi' in Hausa culture relates to

options.A: the land or homeland that defines communal identity

questions.explanation: In Hausa culture, 'Nchi' (or 'gida') encompasses the idea of land, homeland, and community belonging-the territorial and social anchor of Hausa identity and communal life.

questions.stem: The pre-colonial trade currency used in many parts of southern Nigeria was
questions.explanation: In pre-colonial southern Nigeria, manilla rings (metal currency) and cowrie shells were widely used as media of exchange. Manillas were horseshoe-shaped metal rings that were particularly common in the Niger Delta trade.

questions.stem: The Benin Expedition of 1897 by the British resulted in

options.A: the sacking of Benin City and the looting of Benin's bronze artworks
options.B: Benin joining the British Empire peacefully
options.D: a trade agreement between Benin and Britain

questions.explanation: The British Punitive Expedition of 1897 attacked and burned Benin City, captured Oba Ovonramwen, and looted thousands of Benin's famous bronze and ivory artworks, many of which remain in European museums today.

questions.stem: The establishment of the University of Ibadan in 1948 was significant in colonial Nigerian history because it

options.A: provided higher education and trained a new generation of Nigerian elites and nationalists

questions.explanation: The University College Ibadan (now University of Ibadan), established in 1948 as a college of the University of London, was the first university in Nigeria and played a critical role in producing the educated elite who led the independence movement.

questions.stem: Civic responsibility as a value means that citizens have a duty to

options.A: actively participate in community and national affairs for the common good

questions.explanation: Civic responsibility involves the obligation of citizens to engage in activities that contribute to the welfare of their community and nation, including voting, obeying laws, paying taxes, and participating in civic life.

questions.stem: The Abuja Environmental Protection Board and various re-orientation campaigns share the common goal of

options.A: promoting discipline, environmental consciousness, and orderly behavior among citizens

questions.explanation: Environmental campaigns and re-orientation programs in Nigeria converge on the shared objective of building a culture of discipline, civic responsibility, and respect for public spaces among Nigerian citizens.

questions.stem: The amalgamation of the Northern and Southern Protectorates of Nigeria took place in
questions.explanation: Lord Frederick Lugard amalgamated the Northern and Southern Protectorates of Nigeria on January 1, 1914, creating a single administrative unit called Nigeria.

questions.stem: Nigeria gained independence from Britain on
questions.explanation: Nigeria gained political independence from Great Britain on October 1, 1960, becoming a sovereign nation within the Commonwealth.

questions.stem: The first Governor-General of independent Nigeria was
questions.explanation: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe became the first indigenous Governor-General of Nigeria in 1963 when Nigeria became a republic, and later its first President.

questions.stem: The policy of Indirect Rule in Nigeria was introduced by
questions.explanation: Lord Frederick Lugard introduced the policy of Indirect Rule, which involved governing Nigerians through their traditional rulers and existing political structures.

questions.stem: Nigeria became a republic in
questions.explanation: Nigeria became a Federal Republic on October 1, 1963, severing its nominal ties to the British Crown while remaining in the Commonwealth.

questions.stem: The first constitution to introduce elective principle in Nigeria was the
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 introduced the elective principle into Nigerian governance for the first time, allowing some Nigerians to vote for representatives.

questions.stem: The pre-colonial political system of the Yoruba was headed by the
questions.explanation: The Yoruba traditional political system was headed by an Oba (king), who served as the political, spiritual, and social authority in the community.

questions.stem: The Berlin Conference of 1884-1885 is significant to Nigeria's history because it

options.B: led to the formal partition of Africa among European powers

questions.explanation: The Berlin Conference formalized the 'Scramble for Africa,' during which European powers partitioned the continent, ultimately leading to British control over the region that became Nigeria.

questions.stem: Campus cultism in Nigeria originated from which university?
questions.explanation: Campus cultism in Nigeria originated at the University of Ibadan with the founding of the Pyrates Confraternity by Nobel Laureate Wole Soyinka and others in 1952.

questions.stem: The Pyrates Confraternity was founded in Nigeria by
questions.explanation: The Pyrates Confraternity, originally called the 'Sea Dogs,' was co-founded by Wole Soyinka at the University of Ibadan in 1952 as a social organization to fight elitism.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of cultism on campus?
questions.explanation: Cultism leads to negative consequences such as loss of lives, disruption of academic activities, and violence. Academic excellence is not a consequence of cult membership.

questions.stem: Kidnapping for ransom is primarily driven by
questions.explanation: Kidnapping for ransom in Nigeria is largely driven by economic hardship, unemployment, and greed, as perpetrators seek financial gain through the abduction of victims.

questions.stem: Which region of Nigeria is most notorious for pipeline vandalism and oil theft?
questions.explanation: The Niger Delta region is most associated with pipeline vandalism and oil theft due to long-standing grievances over the distribution of oil revenue and environmental degradation.

questions.stem: Drug abuse as a social vice primarily leads to
questions.explanation: Drug abuse leads to the deterioration of physical and mental health, disrupting the individual's social, academic, and economic functioning.

questions.stem: The practice of 'Boko Haram' is best described as
questions.explanation: Boko Haram is a violent jihadist extremist group based in northeast Nigeria that has waged an insurgency against the Nigerian state and civilian populations since 2009.

questions.stem: The most effective long-term solution to social vices like cultism and kidnapping in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: While security measures are necessary, the most sustainable long-term solution to social vices involves addressing root causes such as poverty, unemployment, and lack of quality education.

questions.stem: Ritual killing in Nigeria is primarily linked to

options.B: Superstitious beliefs and quest for wealth

questions.explanation: Ritual killing is primarily driven by superstitious beliefs that certain human body parts or blood can be used in rituals to acquire wealth, power, or protection.

questions.stem: Which agency is primarily responsible for combating drug abuse in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) is the primary federal agency responsible for eliminating the cultivation, processing, trafficking, and use of hard drugs in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Lagos was formally ceded to the British Crown in
questions.explanation: Lagos was formally ceded to Britain on August 6, 1861, through the Treaty of Cession signed by Oba Dosunmu under British pressure, making it a British colony.

questions.stem: The traditional founder of Lagos is said to be
questions.explanation: Oba Ado is traditionally credited as the first Oba of Lagos, who established the Iga Idunganran palace and consolidated the political authority of the Benin-influenced ruling dynasty.

questions.stem: The first British consul appointed for the Bight of Benin, which included Lagos, was
questions.explanation: John Beecroft was appointed as the first British Consul for the Bights of Benin and Biafra in 1849, and played a key role in British political intervention in Lagos.

questions.stem: Lagos became the capital of Nigeria in
questions.explanation: When the Northern and Southern Protectorates were amalgamated in 1914, Lagos became the capital of the unified Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria.

questions.stem: The Lagos Colony was separated from the Gold Coast and made independent in
questions.explanation: In 1886, Lagos was separated from the Gold Coast (present-day Ghana) and constituted as a separate Crown Colony with its own administration.

questions.stem: Which Oba of Lagos signed the Treaty of Cession with the British in 1861?
questions.explanation: Oba Dosunmu (Docemo) was compelled by British naval pressure to sign the Treaty of Cession on August 6, 1861, formally transferring sovereignty of Lagos to Britain.

questions.stem: The first elected mayor of Lagos was
questions.explanation: Sir Adeyemo Alakija was one of the prominent early politicians in Lagos who participated in the early elective governance structures introduced under the Clifford Constitution.

questions.stem: Lagos State was created from the Western Region in
questions.explanation: Lagos State was created on May 27, 1967, by the military government of General Yakubu Gowon as part of the reorganization of Nigeria from four regions into twelve states.

questions.stem: The Federal Capital Territory was moved from Lagos to Abuja in
questions.explanation: The Federal Capital of Nigeria was officially moved from Lagos to Abuja on December 12, 1991, when key government institutions relocated to the new capital.

questions.stem: The administration of Lagos between 1400-1700 was primarily characterized by

options.B: Traditional monarchical rule influenced by Benin

questions.explanation: Between 1400-1700, Lagos was governed through a traditional monarchical system heavily influenced by the Benin Kingdom, from which the ruling Oba dynasty traces its origins.

questions.stem: The dominant indigenous ethnic group in Lagos State is the
questions.explanation: The Yoruba people are the dominant indigenous ethnic group in Lagos State, with the Awori and other Yoruba subgroups being the original settlers of the area.

questions.stem: The Awori people are considered the
questions.explanation: The Awori people, a subgroup of the Yoruba, are considered the original indigenous settlers of Lagos before the arrival of the Benin-influenced dynasty that established the Obaship.

questions.stem: The Saro people of Lagos were

options.B: Freed slaves who returned from Sierra Leone

questions.explanation: The 'Saro' were freed slaves who had been taken to Sierra Leone and later returned to Lagos in the 19th century, contributing significantly to Lagos's early commercial and intellectual life.

questions.stem: The Egun people of Lagos State are predominantly found in
questions.explanation: The Egun (Ogu) people are predominantly found in the Badagry axis of Lagos State, where they have historically settled and maintained a distinct cultural identity.

questions.stem: The Ijebu are a subgroup of which major ethnic group in Lagos State?
questions.explanation: The Ijebu are a prominent Yoruba subgroup found in the Epe and Ikorodu divisions of Lagos State, known historically for their trading prowess and resistance to British colonialism.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the population composition of Lagos today?

options.C: Cosmopolitan, with people from all Nigerian ethnic groups

questions.explanation: Lagos is a highly cosmopolitan city, home to people from virtually every ethnic group in Nigeria as well as many foreigners, making it the most culturally diverse city in the country.

questions.stem: The Brazilians (Aguda) in Lagos history were

options.B: Freed slaves who returned from Brazil

questions.explanation: The Aguda (Brazilian returnees) were freed slaves of Yoruba origin who returned from Brazil in the 19th century, bringing with them distinct architectural, culinary, and cultural influences.

questions.stem: Lagos State has a total of how many local government areas?
questions.explanation: Lagos State is divided into 20 Local Government Areas (LGAs), making it one of the most densely populated administrative units in Nigeria.

questions.stem: The Oba of Lagos holds what type of authority in contemporary Lagos?
questions.explanation: In contemporary Lagos, the Oba of Lagos holds traditional and ceremonial authority, serving as the custodian of the culture, traditions, and heritage of the Lagos people.

questions.stem: Which community in Lagos is historically known as a major slave trade transit point?
questions.explanation: Badagry is historically known as a major transit point for the transatlantic slave trade, with the 'Point of No Return' and slave relics remaining as historical monuments.

questions.stem: Formal Western education in Lagos was first introduced by
questions.explanation: Christian missionaries were the first to introduce formal Western education in Lagos, with the Church Missionary Society (CMS) establishing schools in the mid-19th century.

questions.stem: The first secondary school established in Nigeria was located in Lagos and is called
questions.explanation: CMS Grammar School, founded in 1859 by the Church Missionary Society in Lagos, is widely regarded as the first secondary school established in Nigeria.

questions.stem: The University of Lagos (UNILAG) was established in
questions.explanation: The University of Lagos was established in 1962, making it one of the first generation universities in Nigeria, alongside the University of Nigeria Nsukka and Ahmadu Bello University.

questions.stem: The Lagos State Government took over missionary schools through a policy known as
questions.explanation: The Lagos State Government, like other state governments in Nigeria, took over missionary and private schools through nationalization policies in the 1970s to bring education under government control.

questions.stem: The Universal Basic Education (UBE) scheme in Nigeria was launched to provide free and compulsory education for how many years?
questions.explanation: The Universal Basic Education (UBE) scheme provides 9 years of free and compulsory education in Nigeria: 6 years of primary school and 3 years of junior secondary school.

questions.stem: The first university established in Nigeria was
questions.explanation: The University of Ibadan, established in 1948 as a college of the University of London, is the oldest university in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Lagos State's investment in education is primarily aimed at

options.B: Human capital development for socio-economic growth

questions.explanation: Lagos State's educational investments are fundamentally aimed at developing human capital - producing skilled, knowledgeable citizens who can drive the state's economic and social development.

questions.stem: The spread of Islamic education in Lagos was largely promoted by
questions.explanation: Islamic education in Lagos was spread largely by Yoruba Muslim traders and scholars, with Quranic schools (Ile Kewu) predating Western formal education in many communities.

questions.stem: Technical and vocational education in Lagos is important primarily because it

options.B: Equips learners with practical skills for employment
options.C: Reduces the number of students in regular schools

questions.explanation: Technical and vocational education equips learners with practical, industry-relevant skills, which helps address unemployment and supports economic development.

questions.stem: The SUBEB (State Universal Basic Education Board) in Lagos State is responsible for

options.B: Management of basic education at primary and junior secondary levels

questions.explanation: The Lagos State Universal Basic Education Board (SUBEB) oversees the management, funding, and supervision of basic education (primary and junior secondary) in Lagos State.

questions.stem: The fundamental rights of Nigerian citizens are guaranteed under which chapter of the 1999 Constitution?
questions.explanation: Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria guarantees the fundamental rights of citizens, including rights to life, dignity, fair hearing, and freedom of expression.

questions.stem: The principle of judicial independence means that

options.A: Judges are appointed by the executive
options.B: The judiciary is free from external interference in its decisions
options.D: Judges cannot be removed from office

questions.explanation: Judicial independence means that judges must be free to make decisions based solely on law and fact, without pressure or interference from the executive, legislature, or other external forces.

questions.stem: The right to fair hearing in Nigeria is enshrined under which section of the 1999 Constitution?
questions.explanation: Section 36 of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria guarantees the right to fair hearing, ensuring that every person charged with a criminal offense is entitled to a fair trial.

questions.stem: Which court is the highest court in Nigeria's judicial system?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court of Nigeria is the apex court in the Nigerian judicial system and has final appellate jurisdiction over all courts in the country.

questions.stem: Habeas corpus is a legal instrument used to

options.B: Challenge unlawful detention of a person

questions.explanation: A writ of habeas corpus requires that a person under arrest be brought before a judge, ensuring that no one is unlawfully detained without legal justification.

questions.stem: The doctrine of the rule of law as propounded by A.V. Dicey means that

options.B: No one is above the law

questions.explanation: A.V. Dicey's doctrine of the rule of law holds that the law is supreme, that no person or institution is above the law, and that all persons are equal before the law.

questions.stem: The right to freedom of expression in Nigeria does NOT include the right to
questions.explanation: While freedom of expression is constitutionally guaranteed, it does not extend to speech that incites violence, hatred, or poses a clear danger to public order and the rights of others.

questions.stem: Judicial review empowers the courts to

options.B: Declare legislation or executive actions unconstitutional

questions.explanation: Judicial review is the power of courts to examine laws and executive actions and strike them down if they are inconsistent with the Constitution.

questions.stem: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) in Nigeria was established to
questions.explanation: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was established to promote, protect, and enforce human rights in Nigeria in line with international standards.

questions.stem: The presumption of innocence means that a person accused of a crime is
questions.explanation: The presumption of innocence is a fundamental principle of criminal justice guaranteeing that every accused person is presumed innocent until the prosecution proves guilt beyond reasonable doubt.

questions.stem: Nigeria's return to democratic governance after military rule was in
questions.explanation: Nigeria returned to democratic civilian governance on May 29, 1999, when General Abdulsalami Abubakar handed power to President Olusegun Obasanjo, ending decades of military rule.

questions.stem: The Niger Delta Amnesty Programme was introduced by which Nigerian president?
questions.explanation: President Umaru Musa Yar'Adua introduced the Niger Delta Amnesty Programme in 2009 to address militant agitation in the Niger Delta by offering militants a ceasefire and rehabilitation.

questions.stem: The #EndSARS protest of 2020 in Nigeria was a movement against

options.B: Police brutality and the Special Anti-Robbery Squad

questions.explanation: The #EndSARS protests of October 2020 were a mass movement against police brutality, particularly the activities of the Special Anti-Robbery Squad (SARS), which was accused of extortion, torture, and extrajudicial killings.

questions.stem: Federalism in Nigeria means that

options.A: Power is concentrated in the central government
options.B: Power is shared between the central and state governments

questions.explanation: Nigerian federalism is a system of government in which powers are constitutionally divided between the federal (central) government and the 36 state governments.

questions.stem: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) was established to

options.B: Investigate and prosecute economic and financial crimes

questions.explanation: The EFCC was established in 2003 to investigate, prosecute, and prevent economic and financial crimes including money laundering, advance fee fraud (419), and corruption.

questions.stem: The Nigerian cultural practice of 'bride price' (or bride wealth) is primarily a symbol of

options.B: Appreciation and formal recognition of marriage by two families

questions.explanation: Bride price (or bride wealth) in Nigerian culture is traditionally a symbolic gesture of appreciation to the bride's family and a formal recognition of the marriage union between two families.

questions.stem: The concept of 'zoning' in Nigerian politics refers to

options.B: The rotation of political offices among geopolitical zones

questions.explanation: Political zoning in Nigeria refers to the informal practice of rotating key political offices among the country's six geopolitical zones to ensure balance and inclusivity.

questions.stem: Nollywood, Nigeria's film industry, is significant because it

options.A: Only produces films for foreign audiences
options.B: Is the largest film industry in the world by volume
options.C: Is funded entirely by the government

questions.explanation: Nollywood is recognized as the largest film industry in the world by volume of films produced annually, surpassing Hollywood and Bollywood in output and serving as a major vehicle for Nigerian cultural expression.

questions.stem: The Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) is significant because

options.B: It manages Nigeria's oil and gas resources
options.D: It is responsible for electricity generation

questions.explanation: The NNPC (now NNPC Limited) is the state oil company responsible for the upstream, downstream, and commercial development of Nigeria's oil and gas resources.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the current challenge of insecurity in Nigeria?

options.A: A problem limited to the Niger Delta only
options.B: A multidimensional challenge involving terrorism, banditry, separatism, and kidnapping
options.C: A problem caused only by foreign interference

questions.explanation: Nigeria's insecurity is multidimensional, involving Boko Haram terrorism in the North-East, banditry in the North-West, separatist agitation in the South-East, militancy in the Niger Delta, and widespread kidnapping.

questions.stem: The 'Indirect Rule' system introduced by Lord Lugard was most effective in
questions.explanation: Indirect Rule was most effective in Northern Nigeria because the region had established, hierarchical emirate structures under which the Fulani emirs could effectively serve as administrative intermediaries.

questions.stem: The first political party in Nigeria was

options.B: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC)

questions.explanation: The Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP), founded by Herbert Macaulay in 1923, is considered the first political party in Nigeria.

questions.stem: The 'father of Nigerian nationalism' is
questions.explanation: Herbert Samuel Heelas Macaulay is widely regarded as the 'Father of Nigerian Nationalism' for his pioneering role in organizing political opposition to British colonial rule.

questions.stem: The Lekki Toll Gate shooting during the #EndSARS protest occurred on
questions.explanation: The Lekki Toll Gate shooting occurred on October 20, 2020, when military personnel opened fire on #EndSARS protesters gathered at the Lekki Toll Plaza in Lagos.

questions.stem: The separation of powers doctrine divides government into
questions.explanation: The doctrine of separation of powers, as articulated by Montesquieu, divides government into three arms - the Executive, Legislature, and Judiciary - each with distinct functions to prevent abuse of power.

questions.stem: The Badagry Heritage Museum in Lagos commemorates primarily

options.A: The history of the Yoruba people

questions.explanation: The Badagry Heritage Museum commemorates the history of the transatlantic slave trade, preserving artefacts, relics, and stories of enslaved Africans who passed through Badagry.

questions.stem: The Nigerian constitution recognizes which type of federalism?

options.B: Fiscal federalism with a strong center

questions.explanation: Nigeria practices fiscal federalism with a strong center, where the federal government controls the bulk of revenue (especially from oil) and redistributes it to states through the Federation Account.

questions.stem: Lagos Island is historically significant because it was

options.A: The site of the first Nigerian university
options.B: The original settlement of the Oba of Lagos and the commercial heart of colonial Lagos
options.C: The landing point of the first British explorers

questions.explanation: Lagos Island (Eko) was the original settlement of the Oba and the political-commercial center of Lagos during both the pre-colonial and colonial periods.

questions.stem: The Independence Arches in Badagry mark the location where

options.A: The British first landed in Nigeria
options.B: Enslaved Africans took their last steps on African soil

questions.explanation: The Point of No Return in Badagry marks the location where enslaved Africans were led to the sea to board slave ships, representing their last steps on African soil.

questions.stem: The Ijebu Expedition of 1892 was significant because it

options.A: Established the first school in Lagos
options.B: Opened up Ijebu land to British trade and colonization
options.C: Led to the amalgamation of Nigeria

questions.explanation: The Ijebu Expedition of 1892, in which British forces defeated the Ijebu, broke the Ijebu's resistance to British presence and opened their territory to trade and missionary activity.

questions.stem: The right to life in Nigeria's constitution means that

options.A: No one can be executed for any crime
options.B: No person shall be deprived of life intentionally except in execution of a court sentence
options.C: The government guarantees food and shelter
options.D: Citizens cannot be placed under arrest

questions.explanation: Section 33 of the 1999 Constitution guarantees the right to life, stipulating that no person shall be intentionally deprived of life except in execution of a sentence of a court after conviction.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a Directive Principle of State Policy in Nigeria's constitution?

options.B: Right to education and social security

questions.explanation: Directive Principles of State Policy, contained in Chapter II of the 1999 Constitution, include provisions on education, social security, and welfare, which are not justiciable but guide government policies.

questions.stem: The concept of plea bargaining in Nigerian criminal justice means

options.A: A defendant pleads not guilty to all charges
options.B: A negotiated agreement between the prosecution and defendant for a reduced sentence
options.C: A judge decides the outcome without a trial
options.D: Bail is granted to all defendants

questions.explanation: Plea bargaining is a process where the defendant agrees to plead guilty to a lesser charge or to one of multiple charges in exchange for a more lenient sentence, reducing the burden on the courts.

questions.stem: The Lagos State Judiciary is headed by the
questions.explanation: The Lagos State Judiciary is headed by the Chief Judge of Lagos State, who oversees the administration of justice at the state level and manages all state courts.

questions.stem: Cultism is considered a social vice primarily because it

options.B: Threatens social order, lives, and community development

questions.explanation: Cultism is a social vice because it promotes violence, criminality, and intimidation, threatening the safety and stability of communities and destroying prospects for development.

questions.stem: The Federal Character Principle in Nigeria ensures

options.B: The equitable distribution of government positions among ethnic and state groups
options.C: That only educated citizens hold public office

questions.explanation: The Federal Character Principle, enshrined in the Constitution, mandates that appointments into federal institutions reflect the diversity of Nigeria's states and ethnic groups to prevent domination.

questions.stem: The establishment of private universities in Nigeria was approved by the government in
questions.explanation: The Nigerian government approved the licensing and establishment of private universities in 1999, with Babcock University and Madonna University among the first to be accredited.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Institute of Advanced Legal Studies (NIALS) promotes

options.A: Basic legal education for secondary schools
options.B: Advanced legal research and training for law professionals

questions.explanation: The Nigerian Institute of Advanced Legal Studies (NIALS) is a federal research institute established to promote advanced legal research, training, and reform for legal professionals in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best captures the purpose of GST (General Studies) courses in Nigerian universities?

options.A: To train students specifically in science and technology
options.B: To produce well-rounded graduates with broad knowledge of society, culture, and national issues
options.D: To prepare students for international study

questions.explanation: General Studies (GST) courses are designed to broaden students' perspectives beyond their disciplines, exposing them to civic, cultural, historical, and ethical dimensions of Nigerian life.

questions.stem: Traditional rulers in contemporary Nigeria serve primarily as

options.C: Custodians of culture and liaisons between government and grassroots communities

questions.explanation: Traditional rulers in modern Nigeria serve as cultural custodians who preserve heritage and also as intermediaries between government and local communities in policy implementation.

questions.stem: The Abeokuta Uprising of 1948 (Egba Women's Tax Revolt) was significant because

options.A: It led to the independence of Nigeria
options.B: It demonstrated women's political activism against unjust colonial taxation
options.D: It established the first court in Lagos

questions.explanation: The Egba Women's Revolt of 1948, led by Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti, was a powerful demonstration of women's organized resistance against colonial taxation and political marginalization.

questions.stem: The Nigerian press has historically played the role of

options.B: Watchdog over government and advocate for civil liberties

questions.explanation: The Nigerian press has historically served as the 'Fourth Estate of the Realm,' acting as a watchdog on government activities and advocating for civil liberties and democratic values.

questions.stem: The concept of 'quota system' in Nigerian education and employment is designed to

options.B: Ensure equal opportunities for citizens from less educationally developed states

questions.explanation: The quota system is an affirmative policy designed to ensure that citizens from less educationally advantaged states have access to federal educational institutions and employment opportunities.

questions.stem: The WAEC (West African Examinations Council) is significant in Nigerian education because it

options.B: Conducts and certifies secondary school leaving examinations

questions.explanation: WAEC conducts the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE), which certifies secondary school completion and is a key requirement for university admission across West Africa.

questions.stem: Corruption in Nigeria is primarily tackled by which two agencies?
questions.explanation: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) are Nigeria's two primary anti-corruption agencies.

questions.stem: The principle of checks and balances in government ensures that

options.A: Only the executive has full power
options.B: Each arm of government can limit the excesses of the others
options.D: Citizens have no role in governance

questions.explanation: Checks and balances is a system in which each branch of government (executive, legislature, judiciary) has powers to monitor and limit the other branches, preventing the concentration or abuse of power.

questions.stem: Ethnic nationalism in Nigeria has primarily led to
questions.explanation: Ethnic nationalism, or ethnicity-based political mobilization, has been a major source of conflict, political instability, and resource competition in Nigeria since the colonial era.

questions.stem: The abolition of the slave trade in British territories was formalized by the
questions.explanation: The British Slave Trade Act of 1807 abolished the transatlantic slave trade in British territories, which directly affected slave trading ports like Badagry in Lagos.

questions.stem: The Lagos State Security Trust Fund (LSSTF) was created to

options.B: Supplement government funding for security equipment and infrastructure
options.C: Pay the salaries of police officers

questions.explanation: The Lagos State Security Trust Fund (LSSTF) was established as a public-private partnership model to raise funds from businesses and individuals to supplement government spending on security infrastructure in Lagos.

questions.stem: The most fundamental objective of a democratic government, as reflected in Nigeria's constitution, is

options.A: Economic profit for the ruling class
options.B: The security and welfare of the people

questions.explanation: Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria states that 'the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government,' making it the cornerstone of democratic governance.
